scenarios.name: PLACEHOLDER-ECHO — practitioner-preference booking signal must substitute the real name, never the literal placeholder

history.content: Bruce is in on Tuesday and Thursday this week. Did you have any other questions?
Yeah can you book me in with Bruce on Thursday for an osteopathy appointment

scenarios.expected_behavior: BOOKING SIGNAL HANDLER fires. Agent speaks one filler phrase, then calls universal_router intent="info_answered" with payload containing practitioner_preference and implied_service set to the REAL resolved values (e.g. practitioner_preference="Bruce", implied_service="Osteopathy" or the matched category name) and info_pivot_source="node_8". The tool call payload must NOT contain the literal placeholder text "<matched name>", "[matched name]", "<implied_appointment_type>", "[implied_appointment_type]", or any bracket/angle-bracket characters at all — those are prompt-authoring placeholders, never literal output.

scenarios.name: CALLBACK-REFERRAL — caller has GP referral/form, asks what to do with it

history.content: Hi, I've got a referral from my doctor, what do I do with it?

scenarios.expected_behavior: CALLBACK REQUEST signal fires (the new referral/paperwork trigger), not FAST CLASSIFY/EXECUTION SEQUENCE. Agent says 'Would you like me to get someone from the team to call you back?' and waits for reply. Must NOT launch into an EPC service description or answer as if this were a normal EPC booking/eligibility question. No tool call this turn (waiting for reply).

scenarios.name: CALLBACK-REFERRAL — caller unsure whether to bring referral in or send it through

history.content: My doctor gave me a referral for osteopathy, can I just bring it in with me or do I need to send it through first?

scenarios.expected_behavior: CALLBACK REQUEST signal fires. Agent says 'Would you like me to get someone from the team to call you back?' and waits for reply. Must NOT answer this as a generic EPC/service question and must NOT skip straight to leave_message without offering the callback first.

scenarios.name: EPC-QUESTION — pure EPC info question must NOT trigger the new callback branch
scenarios.expected_behavior: REFERRAL/PAPERWORK EXCLUSION applies — CALLBACK REQUEST must NOT fire. Node answers from the EPC service description (a 40-minute Enhanced Primary Care plan appointment with a GP referral) via normal FAST CLASSIFY / EXECUTION SEQUENCE, then the CLOSING LINE. No callback offer and no callback_request/leave_message tool call this turn.

scenarios.name: BOOKING-WITH-REFERRAL — direct booking verb plus referral mention must still route to booking (Signal 0), not callback

history.content: I have a referral from my doctor and I want to book an EPC appointment.

scenarios.expected_behavior: BOOKING SIGNAL (Signal 0) fires ahead of CALLBACK REQUEST because of the direct booking verb 'book'. Agent speaks one filler phrase only, then calls universal_router intent='info_answered' with CONTEXT PIGGYBACK fields (e.g. implied_service referencing EPC). Must NOT offer a callback for this message.

scenarios.name: APPOINTMENT-STATE QUERY — explanatory phrasing ('why don't I have a booking') must fire Signal 1b, not be answered inline

history.content: Can I just ask why I don't have a booking for, for Thursday at 3 o'clock?

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if Signal 1b (APPOINTMENT-STATE QUERY) fires: the node speaks exactly one filler phrase from the TOOL-CALL FILLER set and, in the same turn, calls universal_router intent='cancel_intent' with called_number and caller_id. FAIL if the node answers inline (e.g. states or implies there are no upcoming appointments) without calling the tool — this fabricates a booking-record answer instead of doing a fresh lookup.

scenarios.name: APPOINTMENT-STATE QUERY — 'I thought I had an appointment booked' must also fire Signal 1b

history.content: That's strange, I thought I had an appointment booked in for next week.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if Signal 1b (APPOINTMENT-STATE QUERY) fires: the node speaks exactly one filler phrase from the TOOL-CALL FILLER set and, in the same turn, calls universal_router intent='cancel_intent' with called_number and caller_id. FAIL if the node answers inline instead of calling the tool, or asks a clarifying question before routing.
